edges.mechanism: High-dose iodine has an additive antithyroid effect and could cause hypothyroidism; conversely excess iodine may reduce antithyroid-drug effectiveness in hyperthyroid Graves' disease. Deliberate KI + methimazole co-therapy speeds FT4 control.
edges.evidence: NIH ODS interaction statement; narrative review; RCT (n=134) of MMI+KI showing faster normalization without thionamide resistance

edges.mechanism: Lithium and excess iodide both inhibit thyroid hormone release (synergistic in rats); KI 250 mg qid in lithium-treated patients raised TSH, causing hypothyroidism in 2/10 and Jod-Basedow hyperthyroidism in 1/10. Iodine status modifies lithium thyroid risk.
edges.evidence: Small human pharmacology study (n=10), rat study, review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Amiodarone is 37% iodine by weight and releases large iodine loads; ~20% develop hypo- or hyperthyroidism (pooled hypothyroidism prevalence 14%). Additional iodide after amiodarone thyrotoxicosis induced subclinical hypothyroidism.
edges.evidence: Clinical review, SR/MA (29 records, n=14,143), small SSKI challenge study

edges.mechanism: Potassium iodide supplies potassium; with ACE inhibitors raises risk of hyperkalemia. Relevant mainly at pharmacological KI doses (mg), negligible at microgram nutritional doses.
edges.evidence: NIH ODS interaction statement; no controlled study

edges.mechanism: Potassium-retaining mechanism shared with ACE inhibitors; hyperkalemia risk with pharmacological KI doses is extrapolated (ARBs not named by ODS).
edges.evidence: Extrapolation from NIH ODS statements on ACE inhibitors/K-sparing diuretics

edges.mechanism: Additive potassium load from KI with renal potassium retention increases hyperkalemia risk.
Iodine does not replace thyroid hormone in established hypothyroidism; in L-thyroxine-treated pregnant women 150 mcg/day iodine did not improve maternal FT4/FT3 and neonatal TSH was 33% higher.
Large additional iodine load; 11.5% developed thyroid dysfunction after contrast in a prospective cohort; neonates most vulnerable. Additive with supplemental iodine in susceptible people.

Genistein inactivates thyroid peroxidase; soy antithyroid effects are greatly increased by iodine deficiency and countered by adequate iodine. Soy raised TSH by 0.248 mIU/L without FT3/FT4 change in RCT MA.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic/animal review plus MA of RCTs (18 articles); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Stacking kelp/seaweed or other iodine-containing products with KI raises total intake above the UL; kelp iodine content is highly variable and has caused transient hyperthyroidism.
Failure to escape the Wolff-Chaikoff effect causes iodine-induced hypothyroidism; high-dose OTC iodine caused severe hypothyroidism in Hashimoto's; adverse effects at intakes safe for others.

edges.with: nodular thyroid disease with heart disease
edges.mechanism: Jod-Basedow (iodine-induced hyperthyroidism) in autonomous nodules; arrhythmia/chest pain risk.
edges.evidence: FDA KI labels (iOSAT, ThyroShield) contraindication; review

edges.with: Graves' disease history or nodular goiter
edges.mechanism: Iodine-induced hyperthyroidism in euthyroid patients previously treated for Graves' disease and in nodular goiter; population iodization increased hyperthyroidism incidence.

edges.with: dermatitis herpetiformis / hypocomplementemic vasculitis / iodine allergy
edges.mechanism: Increased risk of iodide hypersensitivity reactions (rash, angioedema, fever with arthralgia).
Requirements rise (RDA 220 mcg), but high maternal doses (e.g., 12.5 mg/day) suppress fetal thyroid causing congenital hypothyroidism and goiter; repeat KI dosing should be avoided.
edges.evidence: Case reports, Cochrane SR, FDA label, NIH ODS

edges.mechanism: Immature thyroid fails to escape Wolff-Chaikoff; KI label advises thyroid function check after KI; contrast-induced hypothyroidism common in neonates.
Deficiency triples radiation-related thyroid cancer risk (RR 3.2) and amplifies goitrogens; correction lowers TSH/Tg in pregnancy, but rapid repletion can unmask autonomy.
Stable iodine from supplements, kelp or contrast competes with radioiodine and lowers thyroidal uptake; a low-iodine diet (<=50 mcg/day for 4-14 days) is used before RAI.
Physiological (not assay) changes: supplementation lowers Tg and TSH in deficiency; excess raises TSH or causes hyperthyroidism.
Biallelic DUOX2 mutations plus in-utero iodine excess (maternal seaweed) produced delayed-onset congenital hypothyroidism missed by newborn screening.
